function.mechanism: Particulate silicates adsorb moisture and reduce interparticle adhesion, improving powder flow; also used as a filtration aid.
common_food_categories: Other dry formulations requiring anti-caking performance

adi.basis: EFSA 2018 re-evaluation concluded safety of E553a(i)/(ii) could not be assessed with available data and stated the old SCF group ADI 'not specified' for silicates/silicon dioxide is obsolete.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA reported major toxicology data gaps and could not conclude on safety for E553a(i) and E553a(ii) as food additives.

fda.notes: GRAS in table salt under GMP with a 2% tolerance.

adi.basis: JECFA chemical page for MAGNESIUM SILICATE (synthetic, INS 553i) lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (1982 toxicological entry); 2011 entry indicates specifications revision only.

concerns.summary: Case-report literature links silicate urinary stones to magnesium trisilicate exposure history in some patients, although cases without clear exposure source are also reported.
EFSA identified substantial uncertainty due to missing reliable chronic toxicity, carcinogenicity, and reproductive toxicity datasets for the E553a evaluation scope.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA reported very low absorption and no indication for genotoxicity or developmental toxicity in the evaluated silicate/talc data set.
JECFA lists ADI as not specified for synthetic magnesium silicate.
FDA keeps magnesium silicate in GRAS listing for table salt with a 2% tolerance and GMP conditions.

populations: individuals susceptible to renal stone formation
adi_exceedance.notes: Classical ADI exceedance cannot be calculated because EFSA considered the legacy group ADI obsolete and JECFA uses 'not specified'; uncertainty is driven by data gaps rather than a numeric threshold.

risk_assessment.rationale: Under the provided tier rules, EFSA's inability to confirm safety in the latest re-evaluation is the decisive factor for a high tier despite continued FDA/JECFA acceptance and limited direct modern harm evidence.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 concluded safety of E553a(i)/(ii) could not be assessed
EFSA considered historical group ADI not specified obsolete
FDA GRAS status persists with strict use condition in table salt (2%)
JECFA ADI listed as not specified with later specifications-only update
Human safety evidence is sparse and mostly case reports (silicate urolithiasis context)
